subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: For explicit `pty: true` in sandboxed exec, should OpenClaw warn and continue without PTY, or fail the tool call?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the report explicitly allows either warning or error, and failing the call would change sandbox exec semantics beyond a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Warn And Continue
options.body: Emit a clear warning when sandbox mode disables explicit PTY while preserving current non-PTY sandbox execution behavior.

options.title: Fail Explicit PTY
options.body: Reject sandboxed exec calls that explicitly request PTY so callers must choose a non-sandbox or elevated path.

options.title: Adopt Or Replace Fork PR After Decision
options.body: Use the open fork PR as source work only after maintainers decide the warning-vs-fail behavior and required proof.

recommendation.title: Warn And Continue
recommendation.body: Emit a clear warning when sandbox mode disables explicit PTY while preserving current non-PTY sandbox execution behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest history signal for the original PTY support, fallback behavior, and adjacent exec routing/docs decisions.
